title: Introduce air-gapped KMS attestation and RBACv2 migration adapter (private-installer)
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped/on-prem environments require cryptographic proof that the KMS provider used for tenant keys is an approved, on-prem-backed HSM or brokered key service. At the same time, some installers still run RBACv1-style bindings; we need a migration adapter that enforces RBACv2 contracts during upgrade while emitting strong audit evidence that is compact and safe to ship out of the air-gapped site for compliance ingestion.

This PR implements a minimal attestation handshake for air-gapped KMS providers (attestation blob + allowlist verification) and an RBACv2 migration adapter that performs non-destructive policy translation and emits an "audit cohort" record that can be sanitized and batched for export. The goal is to give installers a path to upgrade without requiring live cloud reachability and to provide security teams with verifiable artifacts for policy decisions.

What this changes (high level):
- Adds kms/attestor service used by the private-installer that validates provider-signed attestation blobs and resolves provider metadata against an allowlist bundled with the installer.
- Adds rbac/migration adapter that consumes existing binding manifests (v1) and emits equivalent RBACv2 manifests plus a migration-audit cohort entry per tenant.
- Adds audit/cohort sanitizer that redacts secrets, normalizes timestamps, and replaces machine-friendly operator principals with stable pseudonyms before any export.
- Installer integration: private-installer now has a new --kms-attest-mode flag and a controlled upload workflow that writes cohort files to /var/redwood/cohorts/ for offline transfer.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for attestation blob parsing and allowlist checks
- [x] Migration adapter unit tests covering role/permission translation edge cases
- [x] E2E test in private-installer harness that runs entirely offline
- [x] Audit cohort sanitizer tested with fuzzed operator names
- [x] Documentation in docs/private/airgap-kms.md and docs/rbac/migration-guide.md
- [x] Compatibility shim added so upgrades from older installer versions are non-destructive

Security notes:
- Attestation blobs are validated using provider public keys packaged with the installer; we accept only SHA256-signed metadata and reject any unsigned or expired assertions.
- The cohort sanitizer ensures no raw KMS key IDs or plaintext secrets are present in exported artifacts. Sanitizer replaces KMS key ids with stable hash prefixes (first 8 chars) and drops any encryption context entries that contain tenant PII.

Operational notes:
- The default allowlist is conservative; operators can extend it via an allowlist.yaml provided at install time, which is itself signed by a customer operator key and validated by the attestor.
- The cohort upload path is intentionally file-based; we did not add network transfer helpers to keep the initial MVP air-gap friendly.

Backwards compatibility:
- RBACv1 bindings are read-only during migration; the adapter produces new RBACv2 manifests in a separate directory and never mutates the original manifests in-place. The installer will only swap to RBACv2 if an explicit --apply-migration flag is set.

Related work and tickets: ENG-2142 (migration), SEC-78 (attestation requirements), SUP-4312 (customer support case referencing air-gapped KMS verification).

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Please add a unit test for an expired attestation blob scenario (suggested: travel-forward 48h).
Asha Patel: Added expiration test and documented time-skew assumptions in attestor_test.go; replied that we intentionally treat >5m skew as failed by default.
Claire Ng: Can the allowlist be rotated post-deploy? What is the upgrade story?
Asha Patel: Allowlist rotation is supported via signed allowlist.yaml; added docs and a small helper script in scripts/ to sign/verify lists. See docs/private/airgap-kms.md.

Samir Khatri: The sanitizer should be deterministic so different clusters produce the same cohort pseudonyms for audit reconciliation. Ensure stable hashing with a per-install salt stored under /etc/redwood/seed.
Asha Patel: Implemented stable pseudonym generation using HMAC-SHA256 with installer seed; added tests.
release_notes: Private-installer: Add offline KMS attestation and RBACv2 migration adapter. New CLI flags: --kms-attest-mode, --apply-migration. See docs/private/airgap-kms.md for migration and allowlist rotation steps.
post_merge_actions: Backported attestor parsing to release/2024.12 branch (cherry-pick: a1b2c3d). Ops run: security team rotated default allowlist and published signed v1.1 to internal S3 for partner installers.
notes_for_security_review: Key reviewers: SEC team should review default allowlist entries and verify signer key distribution. Threat model: ensure attacker cannot supply a forged allowlist; require local operator signing and HSM-backed key material for the signer. Recommended: manual audit of any custom allowlist before import.
